title: Probe Distribution Shift x Novel Behavior: Does the Anomaly Detector Fail Exactly When the Anomaly Is New?

original_idea.body: Train a linear probe on one prompt distribution and evaluate detection AUC on progressively shifted/novel distributions, plotting probe reliability vs distributional distance.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Shows activation-probe monitoring fails on the novel inputs it is meant to catch, a starred Open Phil direction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe plus AUC vs distributional distance; inherited methodology, single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused reliability-vs-shift curve; probe training is one dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open weights, single GPU, third-party monitoring scrutiny.

low_compute.reasoning: Linear probe on a small open model, single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe OOD degradation known; the anomaly-coincides-with-shift framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Probe OOD degradation studied; the novelty-coincidence framing may be open.
